root_cause.text: The fbcon_rotate_font() function failed to clear the font buffer pointer when memory reallocation failed, leaving a dangling pointer to a buffer that was too small for the rotated font, enabling out-of-bounds access when subsequent console operations used the undersized buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `kfree(par->fontbuffer)` and adds `par->fontbuffer = NULL; par->fd_size = 0;` before the `kmalloc_array()` call. The original code only freed and reassigned the fontbuffer after successful allocation, but if `kmalloc_array()` failed and returned NULL, the old undersized buffer pointer remained in `par->fontbuffer` while `par->fd_size` was already updated to the larger rotated size. This mismatch allowed putcs implementations to access beyond the actual buffer bounds when printing characters with high character codes to the rotated console.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free and clear the old fontbuffer before reallocating it to prevent memory leaks during font rotation.
intent_record.what: Added three lines before kmalloc_array call: kfree(par->fontbuffer), assignment of par->fontbuffer to NULL, and assignment of par->fd_size to 0.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that any previously allocated fontbuffer is freed and its associated metadata is cleared before attempting to allocate a new buffer. This prevents memory leaks when the font buffer needs to be resized, as the old allocation is explicitly released rather than being orphaned when a new allocation is assigned to the same pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature kfree of fontbuffer to prevent use-after-free or double-free issues in font rotation logic.
intent_record.what: Removed a kfree(par->fontbuffer) call that was freeing the old fontbuffer before assigning a new value to par->fontbuffer.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the deallocation of the previous fontbuffer memory. The old buffer is no longer freed before being overwritten with a new pointer, which will cause a memory leak if the old buffer was dynamically allocated.

The vulnerability requires handling the failure case (when reallocation fails), not freeing the old buffer before attempting reallocation. These are different issues - one is preventive cleanup, the other is error handling for failed allocation.

The group addresses use-after-free/double-free issues from premature kfree, which is a different vulnerability than the root cause. The root cause is about failing to clear a dangling pointer when reallocation fails, leading to out-of-bounds access with an undersized buffer. These are distinct memory safety issues requiring different fixes.

candidates.rationale: When memory allocation fails (dst == NULL), the function returns without clearing par->fontbuffer, leaving a dangling pointer to the old, undersized buffer. This is the direct cause of the vulnerability.

This assignment occurs after kfree(par->fontbuffer) only when allocation succeeds. If allocation fails and the function returns early, par->fontbuffer still points to the freed/undersized buffer, creating the dangling pointer condition.

The premature kfree of the old fontbuffer before confirming the new allocation succeeds means if allocation fails, par->fontbuffer points to freed memory. The fix removes this to prevent the dangling pointer when reallocation fails.

The vulnerable statement is the incomplete error handling that fails to set par->fontbuffer = NULL before returning, allowing subsequent console operations to use the dangling pointer for out-of-bounds access.

This premature kfree of the old fontbuffer occurs before confirming the new allocation (dst) succeeds. If the subsequent allocation fails, par->fontbuffer becomes a dangling pointer to freed memory, creating the vulnerability. The fix removes this early free to ensure the old buffer is only freed after successful reallocation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in lines 49-60. When kmalloc fails at line 50 and dst is NULL (line 52), the function sets err = -ENOMEM and jumps to 'finished' at line 54. However, the critical issue is that ops->fontdata was already assigned to point to vc->vc_font.data at line 34 (src = ops->fontdata = vc->vc_font.data), but ops->fontbuffer is never cleared or reset when the memory allocation fails. This leaves ops->fontbuffer pointing to the old, potentially undersized buffer while ops->fd_size may have been updated to expect a larger buffer. The subsequent console operations would then use this dangling pointer to access an undersized buffer, causing out-of-bounds access. The fix would require clearing ops->fontbuffer (e.g., ops->fontbuffer = NULL) or resetting ops->fd_size when the kmalloc fails at line 52-54.
